title: Contents searches stop at about 100 files with no sign, and the status bar's truncation mark and 'stopped at the time limit' are unreliable
problem: (1) The window shows one row per matching file (src/finder/mod.rs:3007-3016 skip every hit after a file's first), but content_search asks the engine for `limit.max(50) * 4` matches with `per_file: 20` (mod.rs:2999-3006). fff's page is counted in matches (grep/grep.rs:672; `page_limit: limit`, crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:912), so for a common word the 2,000-match page is used up by as few as 100 files: the list shows 100-odd rows with result_limit at 500, and each file is scanned for 20 matches instead of stopping at the first. (2) The only truncation signal is a guess from the row count: `capped = is_searching && before >= search_limit` (src/finder/bars.rs:331-333, shown as `500+ items` at 349); `SearchStats.total_matched` is filled (mod.rs:1413, 3023) and read nowhere. So the contents case reads '100 items' with no hint that more files match. For names the guess is also wrong: the engine truncates first and filters afterwards (`raw.truncate(limit)` at engine.rs:587, then `filter_map(into_hit)` at 590-593, which drops hidden files when Show Hidden is off (1399-1401) and folders that no longer exist (1379)), so a capped search whose top 500 include a few dotfiles returns 497 rows with no '+', leaving out visible matches that would have fit, and a search with exactly `limit` matches shows a false '+'. (3) The time limit is applied per search location: engine.rs:924 passes the full time_limit_secs to every root in the loop at 889, so three locations can take 15 s against a 5 s setting (docs/manual.md:1001 promises one limit). `stopped` (960-962) is `elapsed >= limit && next_file_offset > 0`, but next_file_offset is also non-zero when a page simply filled, so a later root can report 'stopped at the time limit' falsely. (4) When a stopped search has no rows the pane says 'No Results - Try a different name, kind, or search location' (mod.rs:3248-3251), wrong for a contents search cut off by the clock. (5) When a search is capped there is nothing to do about it in place; the only way to see more is Settings > Search engine > Results shown.
proposal: Engine::grep: compute one deadline from `started`; give each root `time_budget_ms = remaining.max(1)` and stop the root loop once the deadline has passed, setting `stopped = true` when a root was cut short by time or left unsearched. Decide time-vs-page from the data: a page is full when result.matches.len() >= page_limit; otherwise next_file_offset > 0 means the time budget (or an abort) ended it. Add `#[serde(default)] pub more: bool` to GrepResponse, set when a page filled, the hit loop broke at `limit`, or a later root was skipped. Engine::search: replace truncate-then-convert with a lazy cut, `raw.into_iter().filter_map(|h| h.into_hit(..)).take(limit)`, and record whether anything was left over in a new `#[serde(default)] pub truncated: bool` on SearchResponse. src/finder/mod.rs `content_search`: pass `per_file: 1` (only the first line is shown) and ask for `limit` files (or `limit + 1` so the cut is detectable). Add `truncated: bool` to SearchStats, drop the unused `total_matched`, and in src/finder/bars.rs use `stats.truncated` for `capped` instead of `before >= search_limit`. Wording: `First 500 items` (keeping the filter variant `N of 500+ items pass the filter`) with a tooltip on `status-text`: 'More items match. Narrow the search, or raise Results shown in Settings > Search engine.' Empty state: when search_stats.stopped is true show 'Nothing found before the time limit' with detail pointing to Settings > Search engine. Optional follow-on: after the count render a link-styled `show-more-results` element that sets a per-search `more_results` flag and re-runs with `filter::FILTER_SEARCH_LIMIT.max(result_limit)` (5,000, the limit a filter already uses, mod.rs:1375-1379), cleared in `set_query` and `end_search`; and append `, still indexing` to the status text while `search_stats.indexing` is true. Update docs/manual.md:142-152, 362.
original_test_plan: Engine unit tests: 30 files each holding the word on 25 lines; grep with limit 10, per_file 1 returns hits from 10 distinct files and `more == true`; with a limit above 30, `more == false` and `stopped == false`. Test the page-vs-time rule through a pure helper taking (matches, page_limit, next_file_offset, timed_out). Lazy cut: build `RawHit::file` values `.env`, `.envrc`, `env.txt`, `environment.md` (no disk access) and check that limit 2 with `show_hidden: false` yields the two visible names and `truncated == false`, and limit 1 yields one with `truncated == true`. Headless UI tests in tests/controls.rs: write 30 files with 20 lines of `needle` each before `Ui::open`; `set_result_limit(60)`, `set_search_contents(true)`, `set_query("needle")`; assert `ui.names().len() == 30` and no truncation text (today 60*4/20 = 12 rows); then `set_result_limit(10)` and assert 10 rows and that the `status-text` label starts with `First 10`. For Show More: write log1.txt..log5.txt, `set_result_limit(3)`, `set_query("log")`; assert 3 names and `ui.exists("show-more-results")`; click it; assert 5 names and that the link is gone; with exactly 5 matches and limit 5 no mark is shown.
original_risks: With `per_file: 1` a file's later matches are never read: fine while the list shows only the first line, but it conflicts with the preview-jump-to-match candidate (and any match-count badge), which wants later hits per file and would need per_file > 1 with a file-based page. Other GrepRequest callers (server, Nushell module) must keep their own values. New serde fields need `#[serde(default)]` so older clients of the control socket keep parsing. One reviewer kept the literal `+` and the other two proposed `First N items`; settle the wording once and update tests that assert the status text (tests/basics.rs:980-1006 and tests/file_ops.rs:974 cover only folder listings and should keep the `N items` form for uncapped lists).

verifier.claim_check:
Read-only review; nothing was run. The core claim holds; several sub-claims are narrower than stated and two proposal items are redundant.

(1) CONFIRMED, and it is the part that matters. `content_search` (src/finder/mod.rs:2993-3028) calls `engine.grep` with `limit: limit.max(50) * 4`, `per_file: 20` (3002-3003), then keeps one row per path (3009-3019). `Engine::grep` passes `page_limit: limit` and `max_matches_per_file: per_file` (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:912-917). fff counts the page in matches: `if all_matches.len() >= page_limit { page_filled = true; break }` (fff-search-0.11.0/src/grep/grep.rs:672-678). With result_limit 500 the page is 2,000 matches, so 100 files with 20 or more hits each end the search. The status bar's only signal is `capped = self.is_searching() && before >= self.search_limit.max(1)` (src/finder/bars.rs:331-333), so about 100 rows read as "100 items" with no mark. `SearchStats.total_matched` is written at mod.rs:1413 and 3023 and read nowhere. docs/manual.md:362 promises "at most result_limit items", so this is not intentional. No test in tests/*.rs touches a contents search or the `+`.

(2) PARTLY. `raw.truncate(limit)` at engine.rs:587 does precede `filter_map(into_hit)` at 590-593, and a search with exactly `limit` rows does show a false `+`. But fff only indexes dotfiles when the root is a git repo (`.hidden(!is_git_repo)`, fff-search walk/ripgrep.rs:23; walk/zlob.rs:21-25), and the default root is Home (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:435-437). So the "497 rows, no +" case needs a git-repo search location or a since-deleted folder (engine.rs:1379). Real, but rare.

(3) CONFIRMED in mechanism, narrow in reach. engine.rs:924 gives every root the full `time_limit_secs * 1000` inside the sequential loop at 889, and fff starts its own clock per call (grep.rs:559), so N locations can take N times the limit; docs/manual.md:1001 describes one limit. `stopped` (960-962) uses whole-search elapsed and `next_file_offset > 0`, which fff also sets on a filled page (grep.rs:691-697), so a later root that fills its page after the limit has passed reports "stopped" falsely. Both need more than one search location and the This Computer scope.

(4) CONFIRMED but minor. mod.rs:3246-3249 shows "No Results / Try a different name, kind, or search location." whatever `stopped` says. The status bar still says "stopped at the time limit" (bars.rs:367-368), as manual:1001 documents.

(5) True, but a feature request, not a defect.

Other corrections:
- The serde risk is moot: `GrepResponse` and `SearchResponse` never go over the wire; src/server/mod.rs:415-435 and 487-506 build their own JSON from hits.
- ", still indexing" is redundant: the status bar already shows "Indexing N files…" (bars.rs:374-380), as do the sidebar footer and the empty state (mod.rs:3238-3245).
- A related gap the reviewer missed: when the scope's relative path contains whitespace, no scope glob is passed (engine.rs:904) and out-of-scope hits are dropped after the page is cut (970-974), so a count-based guess is wrong there too.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Do the core fix; drop the "Show more" link and the ", still indexing" suffix; keep the documented `+` wording.

A. `Engine::grep` (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:854-999)
- Add `pub more: bool` to `GrepResponse`. It is built with `..Default::default()`, so nothing else changes; `#[serde(default)]` is harmless but not needed.
- Add two pure helpers so the rules can be unit-tested:
  - `fn root_budget_ms(limit_secs: u64, elapsed: Duration) -> Option<u64>`: `Some(0)` when the limit is 0 (fff reads 0 as no limit), `None` when the deadline has passed, else `Some(remaining_ms.max(1))`.
  - `fn page_end(matches: usize, page_limit: usize, next_file_offset: usize, out_of_time: bool) -> PageEnd { Complete, Full, Stopped }`: `Complete` when `next_file_offset == 0`; `Full` when `matches >= page_limit`; `Stopped` when out of time; otherwise treat as `Full` (an abort from picker teardown).
- In the root loop, call `root_budget_ms(settings.time_limit_secs, started.elapsed())` before each root. On `None`, set `stopped = true` and break. Otherwise pass the value as `time_budget_ms` and note `root_started`.
- After each root, classify with `page_end(result.matches.len(), limit, result.next_file_offset, budget > 0 && root_started.elapsed() >= budget)`. `Stopped` sets `response.stopped`; `Full` sets `response.more`. This replaces lines 960-962.
- Set `more = true` when the hit loop breaks at `limit` with matches left, or when the outer loop breaks at 993-995 with roots still unsearched.
- `fuzzy_grep` and `multi_grep` build `next_file_offset` by the same rule (fff grep/types.rs:262-275), so one helper covers every mode.

B. `Engine::search` (engine.rs:585-600)
- Add `pub truncated: bool` to `SearchResponse` (it derives Default; the only literal is at 594).
- Extract `fn cut(raw: Vec<RawHit>, limit: usize, needle: &str, show_hidden: bool) -> (Vec<SearchHit>, bool)`: `let mut it = raw.into_iter().filter_map(|h| h.into_hit(needle, show_hidden)); let hits: Vec<_> = it.by_ref().take(limit).collect(); let truncated = it.next().is_some();`.
- Replace `raw.truncate(limit)` plus the `filter_map` with it.
- Do not fold "fff total_matched exceeded the per-root fetch window" (665-669) into `truncated`: `total_matched` counts typo matches that the strict filter then drops, so it would put a `+` on most broad queries.

C. `content_search` (src/finder/mod.rs:2993-3028)
- Pass `limit: limit + 1` and `per_file: 1`. fff's sink stops a file once the cap is reached (grep.rs:129), and the row already shows only the first line.
- Collect distinct files, then set `truncated = response.more || distinct_files > limit` and truncate the rows to `limit`. Both terms are needed: the count misses the whitespace-scope case, and `more` is false when file number limit+1 was the last candidate.
- Leave src/server/mod.rs:477-486 (`per_file: 0`) alone.

D. `SearchStats` (mod.rs:275-282) and the status bar
- Replace `total_matched` with `truncated: bool`; set it from `response.truncated` at 1411-1416 and from C in `content_search`.
- In src/finder/bars.rs:331-333: `let capped = self.is_searching() && self.search_stats.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.truncated);`.
- Keep the `N+ items` and `N of M+ items pass the filter` strings. The `+` is documented at docs/manual.md:148, and "First N" is wrong once results are re-sorted by name or date.
- When `capped`, add a tooltip on `status-text`, using the `.tooltip(|window, cx| Tooltip::new(..))` pattern from bars.rs:130-131: "More items match. Narrow the search, or raise Results shown in Settings › Search engine."

E. Empty state (mod.rs:3246-3249)
- When `self.search_stats.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.stopped)`, show "Nothing Found Before the Time Limit" with detail "The content search stopped early. Narrow the search location, or raise the time limit in Settings › Search engine."

F. Docs
- docs/manual.md: line 126 table (new empty state), 148 (the `+` now also covers contents searches), 335/362 (a contents search lists up to Results shown files), 1001 (one limit for the whole search, across locations).
- CHANGELOG.md: add entries under `[Unreleased]` → Fixed.

Pitfalls
- `time_budget_ms` 0 means unlimited in fff, hence the `.max(1)` on a remaining budget.
- `capped` now follows the stats of the results on screen, not the limit of the search in flight. That is the wanted behaviour.
- Under a filter the limit is 5,000 (mod.rs:1375-1379), so a contents search may read up to 5,001 matching files; the time limit bounds it.
verifier.test_plan:
Engine unit tests go in the `tests` module of crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, following `search_settings_change_content_search` (2252-2306): a temp dir, `Engine::new(EngineOptions { roots, app_dirs: vec![], db_dir: None, watch: false, search: Default::default() })`, then `wait_ready`.

1. `grep_pages_by_file`: 30 files, each with the word on 25 lines.
   - `GrepRequest { limit: 10, per_file: 1 }` gives 10 hits on 10 distinct paths, `more == true`, `stopped == false`.
   - `limit: 100, per_file: 1` gives 30 hits, `more == false`.
   - `limit: 240, per_file: 20` gives 12 distinct files and `more == true`, which pins the page-in-matches arithmetic.
2. `page_end` and `root_budget_ms`, pure, no disk:
   - `(matches 10, limit 10, offset 5, out_of_time true)` is `Full`; `(3, 10, 5, true)` is `Stopped`; `(3, 10, 0, true)` is `Complete`.
   - `root_budget_ms(5, 2s) == Some(3000)`, `root_budget_ms(5, 6s) == None`, `root_budget_ms(0, any) == Some(0)`.
3. `cut`, pure: `RawHit::file` for `.env`, `.envrc`, `env.txt`, `environment.md`. `RawHit::file(..).into_hit` builds the entry from its fields without disk access (engine.rs:1380-1397), as `one_letter_app_hits_dont_flood` (2233-2250) already relies on.
   - `cut(.., 2, "env", false)` gives the two visible names and `false`.
   - `cut(.., 1, "env", false)` gives one name and `true`.
   - `cut(.., 4, "env", true)` gives four names and `false`.

Headless UI tests go in tests/controls.rs, using `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| ..)` (which settles), `ui.names()`, and `ui.snapshot("status-text").label()`. No existing test asserts the `+` or search status text, so nothing pinned changes.

4. `contents_search_lists_a_row_per_file`: before `Ui::open`, write 30 files `hay-NN.txt` with 20 lines of `zebraneedle`.
   - `set_result_limit(60, cx)`, `set_search_contents(true, cx)`, `set_query("zebraneedle".into(), true, cx)`: assert `ui.names().len() == 30` (12 today) and that the label has no `+`.
   - `set_result_limit(10, cx)`: assert 10 names and a label starting with `10+ items`.
5. `name_search_marks_only_real_truncation`: write `zlog1.txt` to `zlog5.txt`.
   - `set_result_limit(3, cx)`, `set_query("zlog".into(), true, cx)`: 3 names, label `3+ items`.
   - `set_result_limit(5, cx)`: 5 names, label `5 items` (today a false `5+`).

The stopped-search empty state can't be reached deterministically in the harness, since the smallest limit is one second of real time. Review that branch by eye, or factor the title and detail choice into a pure function of `(indexing_progress, stopped)` and unit-test it in the mod.rs `tests` module.
verifier.risks:
- A common-word contents search now reads up to Results shown matching files instead of stopping near 100, so it can run longer. The time limit bounds it, and this is what the manual already promises.
- `per_file: 1` rules out a later per-file match count or jump-to-match without raising it again. The page would then need the same `more`-based signal, which this change provides.
- `more` from a filled page means "may be more": the remaining candidates are unscanned. The limit+1 request makes the common case exact; the whitespace-scope case can still show a `+` that turns out to be spurious.
- Name-search `truncated` only sees fff's fetch window (engine.rs:665-669). A query whose strict matches lie beyond the top `(limit*4).max(2000)` fuzzy candidates still shows no `+`. This limitation exists today.
- Stopping the root loop at the deadline means later search locations go unsearched once time is up, where today each gets a full budget. That matches manual:1001, but it is a visible change for multi-location setups; cover it with `stopped` and a changelog line.
- Scope creep: the proposal's "Show more" link, per-search `more_results` state, "First N items" rewording and ", still indexing" suffix should be left out. The first two add state and UI for little gain, the rewording contradicts manual:148 and is wrong after re-sorting, and the last duplicates existing indicators.

orchestrator_notes: 'cancel-content-search' lands right before this one and changes how content searches are started and cancelled in src/finder/mod.rs and the engine; build on it.
